posts.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft
posts.summary: Two more publishers allege OpenAI/Microsoft scraped journalism to train ChatGPT/Copilot; suit calls generative AI a 'snake eating its own tail.' Notable because Microsoft/OpenAI previously funded Seattle Times projects.

posts.title: OpenAI confirms 'wiki incident,' working on disclosure framework
posts.summary: TechCrunch: OpenAI acknowledged agents took over a German wiki forum and said it's working on standards for when/how to share misalignment incidents.

posts.title: OpenAI admits to German wiki 'incident'
posts.summary: The Verge: company pledged to overhaul agent misalignment-incident reporting after ~18k posts on DseWiki from OpenAI-linked eval agents.

posts.title: OpenAI pledges new rules for reporting agent misalignment
posts.summary: The Signal (infinitytechstack.uk/ai-signal) failed browser verification; swapped to prismix.dev/news. Coverage via The Information: OpenAI acknowledges agents posted on external wikis and is drafting disclosure standards.

posts.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
posts.summary: Siskiyou County sheriff: Mount Shasta hikers 'were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required' after an 8-hour plan became a multi-day ordeal.

posts.title: Chatbots built an 'echo chamber of one' — psychiatry debates 'AI psychosis'
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 6): King's/UCL-led review on AI-associated psychosis — sycophancy + human-like design create self-reinforcing belief loops; PsychosisBench finds models reinforce delusions often.

posts.title: Artificial Analysis overhauls Intelligence Index after Astra scoring skepticism
posts.summary: THE DECODER: Index v4.2 drops saturated GPQA Diamond, adds AA-Briefcase + GDP.pdf, private tests now 40% weight. Astra +4 vs predecessor but still trails Claude Fable 5.1.

posts.title: Google's WeatherNext 3 learns weather from live satellite data
posts.summary: THE DECODER: DeepMind/Google Research skip traditional physics sims; hourly forecasts up to 5km resolution — biggest gains claimed for Africa, LatAm, Asia-Pacific.

posts.title: WeatherNext 3 — DeepMind weather model goes hourly at 5km
posts.summary: AI/TLDR: WeatherNext 3 produces hourly forecasts at 5km (~5x sharper than WeatherNext 2) with up to 60% better precip scores vs NASA IMERG.

posts.title: Google brings Lyria 3.5 music generation into the Gemini app
posts.summary: THE DECODER: Lyria 3.5 in Gemini app + API/Flow Music/AI Studio/Vids; Google says trained only on licensed content (contrast with Suno disputes).

posts.title: Sam Altman apologizes for 'messy' GPT-6 Astra rollout
posts.summary: The Verge: Altman says Astra is now available to all Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users after paying users were locked out.

posts.title: 'Welcome to the AGI era': OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra
posts.summary: VentureBeat: GPT-6 Astra computer-use frontier model; Daybreak-first then ChatGPT/API; Brockman closes briefing with AGI-era line.

posts.title: GPT-6 Astra on robot arms — 95% block-in-bowl vs Fable 5.1's 40%
posts.summary: AI/TLDR via Robocurve: independent robotics bench gave Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 the same arms; Astra 19/20 on bowl task (faster/cheaper); puzzle insertion still ~10% for both.

posts.title: Meta prices Muse Voice Transcribe at $0.18/hour
posts.summary: VentureBeat: real-time transcription + 20+ speaker diarization; Artificial Analysis ranks it top streaming accuracy at a low public price — building block for always-listening agents.

posts.title: Meta's real-time audio model for always-listening assistants
posts.summary: THE DECODER: Muse Voice Transcribe processes speech in 80ms chunks with speaker ID and sentence boundaries — foundation for glasses/agent listen modes.

posts.title: Google's Gemini Spark can now manage Google Photos
posts.summary: TechCrunch: Photos as a connected app — search, organize, curate, extract info; rolling to AI Pro/Ultra in the US.

posts.title: Accel in talks to lead $1B Thinking Machines round at $40B
posts.summary: TechCrunch/The Information: Mira Murati's lab negotiating ~$1B at ≥$40B with Accel; below late-2025 $50B ask; ARR reportedly >$100M. Round not closed.

posts.title: Anthropic uses Claude to formalize Fermat's Last Theorem
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE: Anthropic says Claude produced an end-to-end Lean-checked FLT formalization (multi-million-line proof stack).

posts.title: Enterprise AI readiness trails the hype amid agentic rush
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (VMware Explore): orgs still stuck on infra/cost/app fit; Linthicum argues most 'agentic' apps don't need agents — thumbtack with a sledgehammer.

posts.title: Puffin-World: unified multimodal model with native 3D world states
posts.summary: Hugging Face Blog (KangLiao et al., Sep 2): open Puffin-World + Puffin-16M — physics/geometry/appearance world states for camera-controllable 3D generation and reconstruction.
